hypotheses.statement: The migration may have been scheduled to modify public.orders but never attempted it
An analytics session may have held a lock that prevented migration planning

observed_facts.statement: Migration log records indicate statements were applied to tables other than public.orders
Lock monitor records show no waiters on public.orders table
Alert records show orders service objectives were met with no breaches
Pool metric records show connection pool utilization within configured objectives

open_questions.missing_evidence: Migration log record showing statement targeting public.orders table
open_questions.question: What evidence would show a schema migration actually attempting to modify public.orders?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Lock monitor record showing lock on public.orders
open_questions.question: What evidence would show a long-running analytics session holding a lock on public.orders?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Migration log record showing lock wait time
open_questions.question: What evidence would show the migration stalling or waiting for a lock?

summary: Evidence review shows no indication of a schema migration stalling. Migration statements were applied to tables other than public.orders with normal durations. No lock conflicts, alerts, or service degradation were recorded.

timeline.statement: Migration batch 2026-07-19 began applying statements to tables other than public.orders
Lock monitoring showed no waiters on public.orders table
Final migration statement applied to table other than public.orders with normal duration
